cards.explanation: The answer is His own town. Matthew 9:1 says Jesus got into a boat, crossed over, and came to His own town. The text doesn't name the town, so I'm not going to make one up, friends. His own town is the stop this passage gives us.

The answer is faith. Matthew 9:2 says, "When Jesus saw their faith, He said to the paralytic…" The men carried him, and Jesus saw it. I think carrying a whole person on a mat is about as real as faith gets, friends. Nobody does that by accident.

The answer is False. It would be easy to guess the first words are "Get up and walk…" But Matthew 9:2 has Jesus say, "Take courage, son; your sins are forgiven." The command to get up doesn't come until verse 6, friends.

The answer is that they say, "This man is blaspheming!" Matthew 9:3 says some of the scribes said it to themselves. They kept it inside, but it was loud in there, bakers. Blaspheming means speaking against God, and that's what they took Jesus' words to be.

The answer is True. The scribes said it to themselves, and Matthew 9:4 says Jesus knew what they were thinking. Then He asked, "Why do you harbor evil in your hearts?" I've kept a lot of thoughts to myself in my day, friends, and none of them got answered like that.

The answer is that He has authority on earth to forgive sins. Jesus says, "But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins." (Matthew 9:6). He's about to show them with what happens next, friends. Jesus calls Himself the Son of Man (Mark 2:10), so He's talking about Himself here.

The answer is his mat. Jesus tells the paralytic, "Get up, pick up your mat, and go home." (Matthew 9:6). The mat he was brought in on is the very thing Jesus tells him to pick up, bakers. I think that's the best kind of luggage swap.

The answer is False. Matthew 9:7 says, "And the man got up and went home." The men brought him to Jesus, but the text shows him getting up and going home on his own, friends. Jesus had told him, "Get up, pick up your mat, and go home." (Matthew 9:6).

The answer is that they are filled with awe and glorify God. Matthew 9:8 says, "When the crowds saw this, they were filled with awe and glorified God, who had given such authority to men." They saw it with their own eyes, friends. I think it's hard to stay quiet after seeing that.
